RULES THAT HOLD THE COUNT AT 10
Hard cap: 10 turns — 6 main questions + 4 probes, exactly at the cap. A probe is a turn. Never an 11th, however thin an answer is.
Only Q2 (1 probe) and Q3 (3 probes) may probe. Q1, Q4, Q5 and Q6 never spawn a follow-up.
Never re-ask something already volunteered — if Q3's main answer already names the partner and the work, skip probe 1 (conversation ends in 9 turns).
Every branch returns something usable, including every 'No'. No dead turns.
Depth lives in Q3 — 4 of the 10 turns. If the respondent is expansive there, let them talk.
Photo upload is an optional prompt after the close — it is not a turn.

NOTE ON FUTURE READINESS — WHY ONE TURN HERE, AND A SEPARATE SURVEY TOO

The 'listen to a million voices on future readiness' mission needs its OWN instrument: a different audience (teachers, youth, parents, system actors), a different scale, and a different design. 150–250 InvokED alumni will never be a million voices, and bending an impact survey to carry a listening mission usually breaks both.

But one turn belongs HERE, because this audience is different in kind: these are the people whose DEFINITION of future readiness shapes how the sector uses the term. 150–250 senior, articulate definitions is a distinct and quotable dataset — and it bridges naturally from 'what came out of InvokED' to 'where the field is heading'. Treat the answers as narrative source material, not as a representative measure.

STATUS: a separate future-readiness survey is NOT being built for now (Sonal, 2026-07-27). Q6 here is therefore the only future-readiness data being collected — treat it accordingly, and don't let the report imply broader coverage than 150–250 senior leaders. If the million-voices instrument is ever picked up, note that the phrasing here is tuned to senior leaders; a grassroots version needs different language entirely — MItra's usual persona, not this one.
UPGRADE IF REGISTRATION DATA CAN PRE-FILL
Role / org / country are already held for the registrant base. Pre-fill them and Q1 collapses into a confirm-tap, freeing a turn while staying at the cap.

Best use of that freed turn: buy back the perception BASELINE before Q2 ('before your first InvokED, how did you view collaboration?'), which would make the before/after shift measurable rather than self-reported.
